items.title: Circular Motion and Centripetal Acceleration
items.formula: a_c = (v^2)/(r) ...(1) where: v is the body's speed, r is the radius of its circular path.
items.raw:
$$ a_c = \dfrac{v^2}{r} \qquad \text{...(1)} $$
       where:  v  is the body's speed,  r  is the radius of its circular path.

items.title: Circular Motion and Centripetal Acceleration
items.formula: In terms of angular speed: a_c = ((ω r)^2)/(r) = ω^2 r ...(2)
items.raw:
In terms of angular speed: 
      $$ a_c = \dfrac{(\omega r)^2}{r} = \omega^2 r \qquad \text{...(2)} $$

items.title: Angular Displacement and Angular Velocity
items.formula: Δ S = rΔθ ...(3) Dividing both sides of equation (3) by (Δt) gives: (Δ S)/(Δ t) = r(Δθ)/(Δ t) ...(4)

items.formula: Substituting relations (5) and (6) into (4) gives: v_T = ω r ...(7)

Substituting relations (5) and (6) into (4) gives:

items.title: Angular Displacement and Angular Velocity
items.formula: When a body completes one full revolution, its angular displacement equals (2π), so after substituting into equation (7) the angular velocity becomes: ω = (2)/(…
items.raw:
When a body completes one full revolution, its angular displacement equals (2π), so after substituting into equation (7) the angular velocity becomes: 
      $$ \omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{t} $$
       where t is the time for one full revolution, and the reciprocal of this time is called the frequency, denoted by the symbol (f) and measured in units of (revolutions/second) or hertz (Hz). The angular velocity in terms of frequency then becomes: 
      $$ \omega = 2\pi f $$
       This is here called the angular frequency.

items.title: Angular Acceleration and Uniformly Accelerated Rotational Motion
items.formula: The quantity a_T=(Δ v_T)/(Δ t) represents the tangential acceleration; the quantity α=(Δω)/(Δ t) represents the angular acceleration, denoted by the symbol (α)…
items.raw:
The quantity \(a_T=\dfrac{\Delta v_T}{\Delta t}\) represents the tangential acceleration; the quantity \(\alpha=\dfrac{\Delta\omega}{\Delta t}\) represents the angular acceleration, denoted by the symbol (α) and measured in units of \(\text{rad/s}^2\). Substituting \(a_T\) and α into equation (10) gives: 
      $$ a_T = r\alpha \qquad \text{...(11)} $$

items.formula: ω_av = (ω_1+ω_2)/(2) The average angular acceleration is therefore defined as the rate of change of angular velocity per unit time, given by the relation: α_av…

items.title: Question 1
items.text: In uniform circular motion, the tangential speed of the object is: a- constant in magnitude and direction b- constant in magnitude and changing in direction c- changing in magnitude and constant in direction d- changing…

items.title: Answer to question 1
items.text: In uniform circular motion the magnitude of the linear speed stays constant, but its direction keeps changing continuously because it is tangent to the circular path at every point. ✓ Correct answer: b — constant in magnitude and changing in direction
items.jump: Solution
